title: LumenPath Logistics - Implementation Ramp & Access Kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align LumenPath's pilot with Redwood: access provisioning (VPC), pilot scope (5 endpoints), latency SLOs, security checklist and next steps for a week-long trial. Agreed to run a small benchmark and share pricing + security docs.
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pilot pricing spreadsheet, access checklist, and draft SOW by 2026-11-20
Diego Alvarez: Prepare a short benchmark runbook and initial model/sequence length recommendations by 2026-11-19
Brian Tate: Confirm VPC peering window and provide CIDR ranges by 2026-11-18
Priya Sharma: Share SOC2 control contacts and specific compliance questions by 2026-11-19
next_steps: Redwood to provision staging endpoints behind LumenPath VPC (peering) for a 7-day pilot
Customer to provide sample prompt set and typical sequence length by 2026-11-18
Schedule technical deep-dive with SE team (firm date: 2026-11-22 proposed)
Redwood to send security packet (SOC2, ISO, KMS docs)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Diego (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood Platform), Ellen (LumenPath Head of ML), Brian (Infra), Priya (Security), Omar (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick alignment on pilot scope, VPC peering, and security checklist. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll run the kickoff. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Ellen: Ellen here, head of ML at LumenPath.
[00:12] Brian: Brian, infra.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:16] Omar: Omar, product.
[00:18] Diego: Diego from Redwood, solutions eng.
[00:20] Ravi: Ravi, platform eng on the Redwood side.

[00:30] Maya: Cool thanks. The aim for today is to align on the 7-day pilot — access, success criteria, and immediate blockers. We'll also set the next technical deep dive. My assumption, please correct me, is you want to validate latency and cost for an in-app assistant across a sample of requests, right?
[00:45] Ellen: Yes, exactly. We want to replace our in-house inference for a subset of routes and see both cost and latency differences. Our primary worry is tail latency under bursty traffic.
[01:05] Omar: And the timeline is relatively tight — Q1 production decision but we want pilot data by end of November to show to execs.
[01:20] Maya: Ok noted. Diego, can you outline the pilot topology we recommend?

[01:30] Diego: Sure, high level — Redwood will provision three staging endpoints in our hosted environment but accessible via VPC peering. We'll keep them constrained to the models you want to test — probably a 13B quantized variant and a 33B float variant, depending on the workload. We'll also provide token-level cost metrics and latency histograms.
[01:55] Brian: Quick question — is the VPC peering mutual auth? We need to ensure traffic never routes over the public internet.
[02:05] Ravi: Yes, peering is normal VPC peering with route tables, nothing crosses public net. We'll use customer-managed encryption in transit and can integrate with your KMS for keys if you want.
[02:20] Priya: When you say KMS, do you mean we can bring our own KMS / HSM? We have strict key custody.
[02:30] Diego: We support KMS integrations, yes — either bring-your-own or we can use Redwood-managed keys with Customer-managed policies. I'll follow up with the specific KMS flows.

[02:45] Ellen: For the pilot, our typical sequence length is around 400 tokens end-to-end, with peaks up to 1k in some threads. Does that change your recommendations on model size or batching settings?
[03:00] Diego: 400 tokens avg pushes more memory for KV cache. For latency SLOs you might want a smaller quantized model for the UI-fast path, and a larger model for quality evaluation background path. We'll show batching and prefix-caching impacts.
[03:20] Maya: Sounds like a canary pattern — route 90% to fast variant and 10% to high quality. Is that something we can configure from the console?
[03:30] Ravi: Yep, rollouts and traffic-splitting are built-in. We can also set fallbacks if an endpoint exceeds latency SLO.

[03:45] Omar: Cost is also a gating factor — if we push traffic to bigger models the ops team will push back. Can you provide an expected cost delta for the two-model canary?
[03:58] Diego: We'll produce a ballpark per-1000-token cost estimate based on quantization levels. Expect the 13B quantized path to be ~40-60% cheaper than a 33B float path, but we'll verify with your prompt set.

[04:20] Priya: On compliance — SOC2 and audit logs — we need to know what audit trails are available and retention windows.
[04:30] Maya: We have standard audit logs in the console with token-level metadata, and our enterprise package includes extended retention. We'll send the security packet.
[04:40] Priya: Also SSO and RBAC — we need SAML integration and role mapping for devs vs data access.
[04:50] Ravi: SAML SSO is supported; RBAC maps to team roles, and sensitive prompts can be restricted. We'll include the SAML guide.

[05:05] Ellen: For the benchmark, we'd like a simple script we can run from our side that hits your endpoints and reports p95/p99. Does Redwood have one?
[05:15] Diego: Yes, we'll provide a runbook and a small harness you can run from your CI or from a bastion in your VPC. It will include headers to emulate KV cache warm and cold runs.
[05:30] Brian: Network wise we need to schedule the peering in our change window. We can do a peering in the next 48 hours but our infra team needs CIDR ranges and expected ports.
[05:42] Maya: Action item: Brian to provide peering window and CIDRs. Diego will provide the port list and connection verification steps.

[06:00] Omar: Who will own the SLO definitions? We want a 200ms median and 700ms p95 target for the fast path. Is that realistic?
[06:12] Diego: 200ms median is aggressive depending on sequence length; with 400 tokens median is more likely in the 300-400ms range for the quantized 13B on good hardware. p95 700ms may be achievable with batching tuned — but there's a tradeoff cost/latency. We'll run benchmarks to set realistic SLOs.
[06:38] Ellen: We need those numbers to present to the exec team; so please include both cold and warm cache numbers.

[06:50] Maya: Security — Priya, any red flags at this point?
[06:55] Priya: A few questions: key custody (we did mention), audit retention, data residency (we store EU data), and whether Redwood retains request logs beyond the pilot. We also need a point of contact for SOC2 attestation questions.
[07:12] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs, and indicate retention defaults and enterprise options. Also note that for pilot we can set a shorter retention window if that's preferred.

[07:30] Diego: Quick note on logs — we can redact prompt content at rest and provide metadata. There's an option to hash prompts and store only a fingerprint for quality metrics.

[07:45] Omar: Regarding outcome for the pilot: we want comparative cost / latency numbers and a qualitative judgment on answer quality. If both look good, we'll expand to 10 routes in Jan. If not, we'll iterate.

[08:05] Maya: Good. Any stakeholder we missed? Particularly legal or procurement?
[08:10] Priya: Legal will probably want the DPA and data processing terms. We'll pull them in if needed.
[08:18] Ellen: I'll loop in procurement if there's a contract draft.

[08:25] Diego: On the technical deep dive (separate call) we'll walk the infra team through model selection, batching knobs, suggested quantization, and monitoring dashboards. Suggested duration 60 minutes. Proposed date 2026-11-22.
[08:45] Brian: That date works for our infra lead.

[09:00] Maya: Ok wrapping up — recap: Redwood to send pilot pricing and SOW draft, security packet, benchmark runbook. LumenPath to provide CIDRs, sample prompt set, and confirm peering window. Action items noted. Any final clarifying Qs?
[09:20] Ellen: Quick micromisc — when you say "prefix caching" earlier the team heard something like KV cash, but we want a short doc on what that means operationally.
[09:30] Diego: Haha yes KV cache — we'll send a one-pager with examples: warm vs cold, prefix caching behavior, when it's safe to batch, and memory impacts.

[09:45] Priya: Also can we get the contact for the Redwood security SE for direct chats?
[09:50] Maya: I'll include that contact in the security packet.

[10:00] Omar: Timeline check — if we get peering set up by 11/18, then benchmarks run 11/19-11/20, Redwood analyzes 11/21-11/22, and deep dive 11/22. Is that ambitious?
[10:15] Diego: It's tight but doable if CIDR and access are provided promptly. We'll prioritize it.

[10:30] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email and assign the items.
[10:38] Ellen: Thanks all.
[10:40] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: Some terms may be mis-heard (KV cache -> KV cash; SAML pronounced as S A M L). There were short overlaps when Brian and Priya chimed in during the networking discussion.
